article_title: Improving Reading Comprehension Skills with Children's Books through Metacognitive Strategy: The Turkish Context
citation: Erkan Çer, Ertuğrul Şahin. (2016). Improving Reading Comprehension Skills with Children's Books through Metacognitive Strategy: The Turkish Context. Journal of Education and Training Studies. http://dx.doi.org/10.11114/jets.v4i9.1566
title: 42-item multiple-choice reading comprehension test (KR-20 = .91)
description: A researcher-built multiple-choice reading comprehension test developed because existing tests' validity and reliability "were not verified for the Turkish language" and they did not reflect the study books' content. It began as 60 items, was reviewed by linguists, child literature experts and developmental experts, trialed with 161 students outside the research group, and reduced to 42 items after removing four items with item discrimination below .30. Reliability by KR-20 was .91.
requirements: Items must reflect the content of the books read and be appropriate to children's linguistic and cognitive level, as ensured by expert review in the article
constraints: Its validity and reliability are established for this Turkish context and these books, not beyond them
target_learners: first-year (5th grade) secondary school students aged 10-12 in Turkey
examples: Applied to both groups at pre-test and post-test over the 8-week period; correct responses scored 1 point, wrong responses 0
